events.title: Galileo Observes Jupiter's Moons
events.description: Galileo Galilei first observed three of Jupiter's four largest moons (Io, Europa, and Callisto/Ganymede) through his telescope, and on subsequent nights identified the fourth. Together they became known as the Galilean moons.
events.significance: The discovery provided strong evidence against the geocentric model, showing that celestial bodies could orbit something other than Earth, and supported the Copernican heliocentric view.

events.title: First U.S. Presidential Election Held
events.description: The first United States presidential election took place, with electors chosen in several states. George Washington was subsequently elected unanimously by the Electoral College as the first President.
events.significance: It established the foundations of American presidential succession and democratic practice under the new Constitution.

events.title: First Commercial Transatlantic Telephone Service
events.description: Commercial transatlantic telephone service opened between New York and London, with calls carried by radio telephone.
events.significance: It marked a major step in global communications, paving the way for the international telephone network.

events.title: Marian Anderson Debuts at the Metropolitan Opera
events.description: Contralto Marian Anderson became the first African American singer to perform at the Metropolitan Opera in New York, appearing as Ulrica in Verdi's Un ballo in maschera.
events.significance: Her debut broke a significant racial barrier in classical music and was an important milestone in the broader civil rights era.

events.title: Vietnamese Forces Capture Phnom Penh
events.description: Vietnamese troops and Cambodian allies captured the Cambodian capital, Phnom Penh, overthrowing the Khmer Rouge regime led by Pol Pot.
events.significance: It ended the Khmer Rouge's brutal rule, during which an estimated 1.5 to 2 million people died, and began a period of Vietnamese occupation.
